action_criteria.expected_evidence: Husband's history of disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, stereotyped routines and a fixed lunch order with anosognosia, an executive-predominant MoCA, and loss of her work role
action_criteria.label: Structured informant history and bedside cognitive screen scored against the Rascovsky features
action_criteria.rationale: The diagnosis of bvFTD rests on the behavioural features obtained from an informant; the screen documents the cognitive profile.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Severe executive and social-cognition deficits on education-adjusted norms with relatively preserved memory and visuospatial function
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological battery including executive and social-cognition measures
action_criteria.rationale: Quantifies the executive and social-cognition profile against her superior premorbid ability, where a screening total understates the deficit.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No reversible cause; TSH normal on levothyroxine
action_criteria.label: Reversible-cause blood tests: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, ESR, CRP
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild frontal and anterior temporal atrophy disproportionate for age with preserved hippocampi and posterior cortex
action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the frontal and anterior temporal atrophy pattern and excludes structural and vascular causes.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left-predominant frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism or hypoperfusion with posterior sparing
action_criteria.label: FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism with posterior sparing supports FTD over AD.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Negative amyloid PET or a CSF profile not consistent with Alzheimer pathology
action_criteria.label: AD biomarker (amyloid PET or CSF Abeta42/p-tau) when AD remains in the differential
action_criteria.rationale: Onset at 52 with a father diagnosed with Alzheimer disease keeps early-onset AD in the differential; a negative study makes Alzheimer pathology unlikely.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pathogenic variant in C9orf72, GRN or MAPT
action_criteria.label: Genetic counselling and FTD gene panel (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT)
action_criteria.rationale: Young onset makes a genetic cause possible even without FTD in the family; testing follows counselling and does not change the clinical diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serotonin toxicity risk with sumatriptan; no interaction with levothyroxine
action_criteria.label: Interaction check before starting an SSRI for disinhibition and compulsive behaviour
action_criteria.rationale: She takes sumatriptan, which carries a serotonin toxicity interaction with SSRIs.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on distinguishing FTD from Alzheimer disease
action_criteria.label: Literature search on young-onset FTD versus early-onset AD
action_criteria.rationale: General evidence only; it does not change the work-up of this patient.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable). Base it on her husband's account rather than her self-report, given her lack of insight.

Explain why early-onset Alzheimer disease (paternal history, repetitive questions) and Hashimoto encephalopathy (known Hashimoto thyroiditis) are less likely, and that amyloid PET or CSF AD markers can settle the Alzheimer question.
Address safety and capacity: fitness to return to legal practice and protection of her clients, driving, finances, and lasting power of attorney while she can still take part.
Offer genetic counselling before any genetic test, and discuss what a result would mean for relatives.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET, or perfusion SPECT where FDG-PET is unavailable, is the functional study when one is needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic, young-onset

differential.diagnosis: Early-onset Alzheimer disease, behavioural or dysexecutive presentation
differential.key_features: For: onset at 52, father with probable AD, repetitive questions. Against: preserved episodic memory and hippocampi, frontal-predominant atrophy with posterior sparing; an optional amyloid or CSF study settles it.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder or occupational burnout
differential.key_features: Against: new progressive behavioural change with loss of empathy and stereotypies, severe social-cognition deficits and frontal atrophy.

differential.diagnosis: Steroid-responsive encephalopathy with autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto encephalopathy)
differential.key_features: For: Hashimoto thyroiditis. Against: slowly progressive course without fluctuation, seizures, myoclonus or confusion, and lobar atrophy; antithyroid antibodies are expected in Hashimoto thyroiditis and do not establish encephalopathy.
Normal white matter; no vascular risk factors.

key_clinical_evidence: Husband's history over 14 months: tactless remarks and inappropriate emails, apathy, indifference to others, repetitive viewing and shopping loops and a fixed lunch order, with anosognosia and loss of her work role.
Severe executive and social-cognition deficits on education-adjusted norms, far below her estimated superior premorbid ability, with relatively preserved memory and visuospatial function.
MRI: mild frontal and anterior temporal atrophy disproportionate for age, with preserved hippocampi and posterior cortex.
The frontal and anterior temporal pattern with relative posterior sparing makes Alzheimer disease less likely; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
If obtained, a negative amyloid study makes Alzheimer pathology unlikely; it does not exclude FTLD.

Young-onset frontotemporal dementia vers.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. FDG-PET with frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism and posterior cingulate sparing favours FTD; amyloid PET or CSF AD markers help when Alzheimer disease remains possible. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

metadata.notes: Probable bvFTD with onset at 52 in a corporate attorney with superior premorbid ability, anosognosia, treated Hashimoto thyroiditis and a father diagnosed with probable Alzheimer disease. patient.history_present_illness: Ms. C is a 53-year-old corporate attorney who presents to the cognitive neurology clinic with her husband. She was placed on a leave of absence by her law firm 3 months ago following a series of uncharacteristic professional errors and interpersonal incidents. Her husband describes a 14-month history of progressive changes that began with what he initially interpreted as burnout. She began asking repetitive questions about case details she had clearly reviewed minutes earlier. She stopped preparing for client meetings in her customarily meticulous manner. She sent a series of unusually terse and inappropriate emails to colleagues. More significantly, over the past 8 months, he has observed a profound shift in her personality: she has become socially withdrawn, showing little interest in their two children's activities, and has made remarks at social gatherings that are uncharacteristically tactless — including commenting on another guest's physical appearance in a way that caused significant offense. She appears indifferent to the social consequences of her statements and shows minimal concern about having been placed on leave, which her husband finds deeply disturbing given how central her legal career was to her identity. She has developed a habit of watching the same documentary series repeatedly and insists on the same lunch order every day. She spends hours on online shopping without making purchases, getting stuck in loops. She herself describes everything as 'fine' and attributes her work difficulties to 'stress and the demanding partners.' Her father had dementia diagnosed as probable Alzheimer's at age 67. She is known to have Hashimoto's thyroiditis with well-controlled hypothyroidism on levothyroxine.

neurological_exam.additional: Her firm placed her on leave due to performance concerns. She has reportedly been making errors in legal documents that she does not recognize or acknowledge. Her husband reports she has been asking the same legal questions to colleagues repeatedly. She remains able to carry out familiar procedural legal routines but shows impaired judgment and reduced insight. Her father had dementia attributed to probable Alzheimer's disease, and she has Hashimoto's thyroiditis on levothyroxine.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but apathetic. She is markedly anosognosic: states she has 'some stress' but no cognitive problems.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone, bulk, and strength 5/5 throughout. No tremor. No rigidity.
